card_overview_title.title:
Diff, validate and label
circuit-tracer circuits
card_overview_title.body: Attribution graphs show where influence flows. circuitcheck asks what training changed, whether the features cause the behaviour, and what each feature does.

card_overview_end.title: pip install circuitcheck
card_overview_end.body: Docs, notebooks and the five-minute quickstart: github.com/albertlieyingadrian/circuitcheck

card_validate_title.title: Switch or readout?
card_validate_title.body: A graph ranks features by influence. The validator switches them off, pushes them and patches them, each against random and size-matched controls.

card_validate_end.title: The graph's top features are readouts
card_validate_end.body: Live on the RL-hack Qwen3-1.7B (3 comment slots) and the password-locked Qwen3-8B (2 questions): switched off together, the graph's ten features are a readout every time, as in episodes 1 and 2. Alone, one feature passes the switch rule once, at the p-value floor: about what chance gives in 33 tests.

card_diff_title.title: What did training change?
card_diff_title.body: Compare attribution graphs of the same prompts before and after fine-tuning or RL, with a random null, a stability check and a validity check.

card_diff_end.title: Same ten features as the study
card_diff_end.body: 9 of 10 specific to the run that hacked, 6 replicated in another seed, reconstruction error unchanged by RL. Caveat built in: the transcoders were trained on the base model.

card_labels_title.title: Cheap labels you can check
card_labels_title.body: Claude Haiku 5.5 labels each feature from its top examples; a detector then scores the label on held-out examples it never saw.

card_labels_end.title: Neuronpedia-level labels for $0.26
card_labels_end.body: 50 Gemma-2-2B features: detection AUROC 0.80 (Neuronpedia: 0.78 / 0.80), simulation r 0.45 (0.37 / 0.38). Every reply cached; export in Neuronpedia's format.

card_walkthrough_title.title:
A graph says these ten
features do it. Do they?
card_walkthrough_title.body: circuit-tracer ranks features by influence on one prompt. In two studies the top ten turned out to be readouts: switch them off and the behaviour stays. circuitcheck tests that, compares graphs across training, and labels features with a trust score.

card_walkthrough_end.title: Test the claim before you publish it
card_walkthrough_end.body: validate: switch or readout, against controls. diff: what training changed, against a null. label: cheap labels with held-out scores. github.com/albertlieyingadrian/circuitcheck
